clue.text: Full of energy; they can go from race to race without losing

definitions.meaning: rechargeable batteries store electrical charge, so they are full of energy

definitions.text: they can go from race to race without losing
definitions.meaning: a multiple bet whose winnings roll on to the next race, lost only if one leg fails

explanation.surface: A tireless competitor who moves from one race to the next and never loses.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage batteries hold charge, and in betting the name is for a wager carried forward race by race while every selection keeps winning.

clue.text: A shock to Eastern Venus, so-called

parts.note: a start is a sudden jolt of surprise
E is the standard abbreviation for East or Eastern

explanation.surface: Someone from the East gets a jolt on meeting a so-called Venus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' marks a loose equation: the Phoenician fertility goddess was identified by classical writers with Venus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoenician goddess of love and fertility was equated by Greeks and Romans with Aphrodite, the Roman goddess of love.

clue.text: Hymn tune's copyright is with Lahore composer

parts.note: C, as in the circled symbol, stands for copyright

indicators.note: a composer arranges things, so the letters of the city name are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A hymn melody turns out to belong, by copyright, to a composer from Lahore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composer' looks like a person from Lahore, but it is the signal to rearrange LAHORE into HORALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately harmonised hymn melody, of the Lutheran kind Bach set, is the classic example.

clue.text: Obsession of doctor that nobody is really fit when up!

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a common crossword doctor
no man means nobody at all

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: A1 means first-class or in top condition, written as A and the letter I

explanation.surface: A doctor gloomily declares that nobody is truly healthy at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written AI, which 'when up' turns to IA at the foot of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixation on a single subject or idea is a mental preoccupation of one thing only.

clue.text: Stop obstruction of service to Uttar Pradesh

parts.note: in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed
UP is the abbreviation for the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh

explanation.surface: Something holds up a service running to the Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' reads like a train or postal service, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A pause or easing off is a halt in some activity, as in rain without a break.

clue.text: Health-giving cookery device

definitions.meaning: one who gives a health, an old word for a drink proposed to someone's wellbeing
a kitchen appliance that browns bread

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget is praised as good for you.
explanation.definitionFit: One who raises a glass proposing someone's health, and the electric appliance for browning bread slices.

clue.text: One of three coming before the law in Berkshire

definitions.text: One of three coming before the law
definitions.meaning: a parliamentary bill is read three times before it becomes an Act
a large town in the English county of Berkshire

explanation.surface: Something in Berkshire is one of three to appear before the law.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament a bill passes three formal stages of debate before becoming law. Berkshire is a county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Each formal stage of a bill's passage through Parliament has this name, which is also that of Berkshire's county town.

clue.text: Organization supplying female underwear

parts.note: a body is an organised group, as in a governing body
stocking means keeping goods on hand to supply

explanation.surface: A firm that supplies women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece garment covering the torso and legs, worn by women as lingerie or for dance.

clue.text: Sort of Pagan creed preferred by Wordsworth

definitions.text: Sort of Pagan creed preferred by Wordsworth

parts.words: Sort of Pagan creed preferred by Wordsworth
parts.note: points to the sonnet 'The World Is Too Much with Us', where the poet would rather be a Pagan suckled in a creed of a certain kind

explanation.surface: A question about which pagan belief Wordsworth favoured.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is 'Great God! I'd rather be / A Pagan suckled in a creed outworn', so the word is the adjective he attaches to that creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete or worn out by long use, describing a belief that has had its day.

clue.text: Ace Kate concealed shows delicacy

indicators.note: the letters are disguised, their true order concealed by being jumbled up

explanation.surface: Kate, a champion, keeps something hidden and reveals a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concealed' signals that ACE KATE is a disguised arrangement of the answer's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet toasted bun with currants is a small treat, served with afternoon tea in Britain.

clue.text: Kind of recognition one does not get through the normal channels

definitions.text: Kind of recognition one does not get through the normal channels

parts.words: Kind of recognition one does not get through the normal channels
parts.note: the normal channels are the five senses, so this perception comes from beyond them

explanation.surface: An acknowledgement that arrives by unofficial routes rather than proper channels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channels' reads as bureaucratic routes; here it means the senses, sight, hearing and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Perception claimed to work beyond sight, hearing, touch, taste and smell, as in telepathy.

clue.text: Where pirates' victims often suffered suspense

definitions.text: Where pirates' victims often suffered suspense

parts.words: Where pirates' victims often suffered suspense
parts.note: suspense is taken literally as hanging: the spar end from which people were hanged at sea

explanation.surface: Pirates' captives endured anxious waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspense' looks like anxious waiting, but it means being suspended by a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer end of a ship's horizontal spar, traditionally the spot for hanging mutineers and captives.

clue.text: Country-lover smashes trap, but there's nothing in it

indicators.note: smashing breaks a thing into pieces, so the word trap is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

indicators.note: the nothing goes inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A nationalist wrecks a trap and finds it empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashes' turns TRAP into PATR; then O is put 'in' IT to make IOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to their homeland loves their nation.

clue.text: Location for the Army Corps

parts.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Somewhere suitable for an army corps to be stationed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers, abbreviated RE, are a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun this adverb means that place, as in 'from here to over yonder'.

clue.text: State gets new CIA guarantee, bumping off the leader with case. I hear

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'State gets new CIA guarantee, bumping off the leader with case. I hear', looks garbled by OCR: an anagram of CIA plus GUARAN(TEE) gives the letters, but 'the leader with case. I hear' fits no parse and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: State gets new CIA guarantee, bumping off the leader with case. I hear

clue.text: Getting together for a meal

definitions.meaning: collecting and comparing items, as in gathering pages into order
a light repast, often cold, served informally

explanation.surface: People gather to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers assembling texts or pages in sequence and also a light buffet supper.

clue.text: Repetitive correspondence carried on by knights of old?

definitions.meaning: letters each recipient must copy and send on to others

definitions.text: carried on by knights of old?
definitions.meaning: armour of interlinked metal rings worn by medieval knights

explanation.surface: Medieval knights kept up a tedious exchange of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carried on' suggests continuing a correspondence; really it means worn on the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the round-robin letter passed endlessly onward and the linked-ring armour of medieval warriors.

clue.text: Originating from a notion by Prospero's brother

indicators.note: the answer originates from these letters, worked up out of them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An idea is credited to the brother of Prospero.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, the usurping Duke of Milan is Prospero's brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Tempest names the usurping Duke of Milan, who exiled his sibling to the island.

clue.text: Undress? Yes, but put this on!

definitions.text: Undress? Yes, but put this on!

parts.words: Undress? Yes, but put this on!
parts.note: undress here is the noun for informal or partial attire, so the garment is a kind of undress you wear

explanation.surface: Told to strip, a person is handed something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undress' as a noun means state of being lightly or casually clothed, as in 'in a state of undress'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's light, flimsy dressing gown is informal attire worn around the house or bedroom.

clue.text: Joint with slice initially cut off may turn bad

indicators.note: the opening letter of slice is removed from the joint of meat

parts.note: a saddle of lamb or mutton is a cut of meat

indicators.note: initially points at the first letter of slice

explanation.surface: A joint of meat with a slice removed may go off.
explanation.walkthrough: SADDLE is a butcher's joint; 'initially' takes S from 'slice', and 'cut off' removes it to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs that go rotten are said to spoil in this way.

clue.text: New order makes it clear to apprentice

indicators.note: a new order for the letters means rearranging the words it and clear

explanation.surface: A fresh instruction spells things out for a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New order' looks like a command; it signals rearranging IT CLEAR. The definition is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To bind someone by indentures as a trainee, as with an articled clerk in a law firm.

clue.text: Jolly or dull, this cleaner?

parts.note: a jolly or a do is a party or festive outing
taken as written
mat, also spelt matt, means without shine

explanation.surface: Asks whether this cleaner is cheerful or boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a party, a do. 'Cleaner' is the thing you wipe your shoes on.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat at an entrance cleans shoes as people come in, wiping off dirt.

clue.text: A whole number for example in Bury?

indicators.note: the abbreviation goes inside the word for burying

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
EG, exempli gratia, means for example

explanation.surface: Asks about a number, perhaps in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bury' looks like the Lancashire town but is the verb, to inter.
explanation.definitionFit: A number with no fractional part, such as seven or minus three.

clue.text: Raise standard of golf shot?

definitions.meaning: to hoist a flag up a pole
a low approach shot that rolls toward the green

explanation.surface: Asks whether a golfing stroke can lift standards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a level of quality; here it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to hoist a flag aloft; as a noun, a low chip in golf that bounces and rolls on to the green.

clue.text: Measure particles by these processes

parts.note: an act of Parliament is a legislative measure
ions are charged atomic particles

explanation.surface: A scientist measures particles by certain procedures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' reads as a verb but is the noun, a law or Act.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeds or operations performed are steps in a course of doing something.

clue.text: This Violet used to comfort Bums

definitions.text: This Violet used to comfort Bums

parts.words: This Violet used to comfort Bums
parts.note: names the purple antiseptic dye once applied to soothe skin burns; the word before violet is wanted

explanation.surface: A woman called Violet who used to comfort the down-and-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'Violet' looks like a woman's name; it is the dye named after a blue mountain flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple antiseptic dye takes its name from the blue alpine flower, and was once dabbed on skin injuries.

clue.text: Immigrant the Revenue run after

indicators.note: the run letter is placed after the word for revenue

parts.note: revenue is income, money coming in
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The tax authorities chase after a newcomer to the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Revenue' suggests the British tax office; here it just means income.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer who moves into a place from elsewhere, an arrival settling in a district.

clue.text: Firm answering for third party in court case

parts.note: CO, company, is a firm
respondent means replying or answering

explanation.surface: A firm stands for a third party in a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In an old English divorce suit, this was the person accused of adultery with the spouse being sued.
explanation.definitionFit: In divorce proceedings on grounds of adultery, the lover named alongside the accused spouse was joined as a defendant.
